sections.title: Part 1: Photographs
sections.instructions: You will hear 6 short statements about a photograph. Choose the statement that best describes what you see in the photograph.
sections.transcript: Narrator: Directions: For each question, you will hear four short statements about a photograph. They will not be printed in your test book and will be spoken only one time. Select the statement that best describes what you see in the photograph and mark your answer.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the photograph?
options: A man is typing on a laptop at a desk.
A woman is watering plants in a garden.
A child is playing with a ball on the grass.
A dog is sleeping on a sofa.
questions.answer: A man is typing on a laptop at a desk.
questions.explanation: The photograph shows a man working at a desk with a laptop, typing on the keyboard.

sections.title: Part 3: Conversations
sections.instructions: You will hear 13 conversations between two or three people. Each conversation will be spoken only one time and will not be printed in your test book. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say. Select the best response to each question.
sections.transcript:
Narrator: Directions: You will hear some conversations between two or three people. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say in each conversation. Select the best response to each question.

--- Conversation 1 ---
Man: Hi, I'm calling about the apartment listing on Maple Street. Is it still available?
Woman: Yes, it is. It's a two-bedroom unit with one and a half baths. The rent is $1,800 per month.
Man: Does that include utilities?
Woman: Water and trash are included, but electricity and internet are separate. The security deposit is one month's rent.
Man: That sounds reasonable. When can I schedule a viewing?
Woman: I have an opening this Saturday at 10 AM or Monday at 2 PM. Which works better for you?
Man: Saturday morning would be perfect. Also, is parking included?
Woman: Yes, there's one assigned parking space. A second space is available for $50 per month.

--- Conversation 2 ---
Woman: Tom, did you get a chance to look at the budget report I sent over?
Man: Yes, I reviewed it this morning. The Q3 expenses are higher than projected, especially in the marketing department.
Woman: I noticed that too. The ad campaign costs went over by about 15%. Should we adjust the Q4 budget to compensate?
Man: I think we should. Let's reduce the marketing allocation by 10% and reallocate that to R&D. We need to invest more in product development.
Woman: Agreed. I'll revise the numbers and send you the updated version by Wednesday.
Man: Great. Also, let's schedule a meeting with the finance team to discuss this on Thursday at 3 PM.

--- Conversation 3 ---
Man: Excuse me, I'm looking for a gift for my mother's birthday. She loves gardening.
Woman: How about this ceramic pot set? It comes with three pots in different sizes. It's on sale for $35.
Man: That's nice, but she already has a lot of pots. Do you have anything else?
Woman: We have these gardening gloves and a kneeling pad set for $22, or this engraved trowel set for $45.
Man: The engraved trowel set sounds special. Can I get it gift-wrapped?
Woman: Absolutely, gift wrapping is free. It'll take about ten minutes. Would you like to add a card?
Man: Yes, please. I'll write a message while I wait.

--- Conversation 4 ---
Woman: Hi, I need to return this jacket. I bought it last week but it doesn't fit properly.
Man: Do you have your receipt?
Woman: Yes, right here. I paid with a credit card.
Man: The jacket is in perfect condition, so a full refund is no problem. Would you like the refund on the same card or store credit?
Woman: Store credit would be fine, actually. I saw a scarf I'd like to buy instead.
Man: Great choice. The scarf is $28, and your refund is $65, so you'll have $37 remaining on your store credit.
Woman: Perfect. I'll take the scarf now and use the rest later.

--- Conversation 5 ---
Man: Good morning, this is Dr. Patel's office. How can I help you?
Woman: Hi, I'd like to schedule a check-up. I haven't been in for about a year.
Man: Are you experiencing any specific symptoms, or is this just a routine visit?
Woman: Just a routine check-up. But I have been having some headaches lately, so maybe I should mention that to the doctor.
Man: I see. Dr. Patel has an opening next Tuesday at 10 AM or Thursday at 3 PM. Which would you prefer?
Woman: Tuesday at 10 works for me. My name is Sarah Johnson, and my date of birth is March 15, 1988.
Man: Thank you, Ms. Johnson. I've booked you for Tuesday at 10 AM. Please arrive 15 minutes early to fill out paperwork.

--- Conversation 6 ---
Woman: James, the client presentation is next Monday. Where are we on the slides?
Man: I've finished the first ten slides covering the market analysis. I still need to add the financial projections and the conclusion.
Woman: How long do you think that will take?
Man: If I focus on it today and tomorrow, I should have it done by Friday afternoon. Can you review the design and formatting over the weekend?
Woman: Sure. I'll also prepare the handouts. Do we need to print copies for everyone?
Man: Let's print twenty copies to be safe. The meeting room is on the fifth floor, right?
Woman: Yes, Conference Room 5A. The client arrives at 2 PM, so let's be there by 1:30 to set up.

--- Conversation 7 ---
Man: I can't believe the train is delayed again. I'm going to be late for my 9 AM meeting.
Woman: There was a signal problem at the Central Station. They said it should be resolved in about twenty minutes.
Man: Twenty minutes? That means I won't get to the office until 9:15 at the earliest. Should I call my boss?
Woman: Definitely. You should let her know. Do you have her number?
Man: It's in my phone, but the battery is almost dead. Could I borrow yours?
Woman: Of course. Here you go. Do you know if there's a shuttle bus alternative?
Man: I checked the app, but the next shuttle isn't for another 30 minutes. I'll just wait for the train.

--- Conversation 8 ---
Woman: Welcome to the Riverside Cafe. Are you ready to order, or do you need a few more minutes?
Man: I think I'm ready. I'll have the grilled salmon with a side salad.
Woman: Excellent choice. Would you like the salad with vinaigrette or ranch dressing?
Man: Vinaigrette, please. And could I get a cup of coffee as well?
Woman: Sure. Decaf or regular?
Man: Regular, with a little milk. Also, does the salmon come with rice or potatoes?
Woman: It comes with your choice of jasmine rice or roasted potatoes.
Man: I'll go with the roasted potatoes. And could we get the check when you bring the food? I'm a bit short on time.
Woman: Of course, I'll bring it with your meal.

--- Conversation 9 ---
Man: Maria, I wanted to talk to you about the new software system. How's the team adjusting?
Woman: It's been a bit of a challenge, to be honest. About half the team is still struggling with the new interface.
Man: I expected that. That's why I scheduled a training session for next week. Would you be able to lead it?
Woman: I could, but I think it would be better if someone from the IT department did it. They know the system inside out.
Man: That's a fair point. I'll reach out to IT. In the meantime, could you put together a quick reference guide for the team?
Woman: I already started one. I should have it ready by Friday. I'll email it to everyone and post it on the shared drive.
Man: Perfect. Let's also set up a feedback session in two weeks to see how everyone is doing.

--- Conversation 10 ---
Woman: I'm thinking about taking a few days off next month. I have some vacation days I need to use before the end of the year.
Man: That sounds like a good idea. Which dates were you thinking?
Woman: I was hoping to take off from the 12th to the 16th. That's the week before the product launch, so it should be quiet.
Man: Let me check the schedule. Actually, we have a vendor meeting on the 14th that you should probably attend. Could you shift your dates?
Woman: How about the following week, the 19th to the 23rd?
Man: That works. I'll approve it right now. Don't forget to submit the formal request through the HR portal.
Woman: I'll do that today. Who will cover for me while I'm away?
Man: I'll ask Kevin to handle your urgent tasks. I'll make sure he's briefed before you leave.

--- Conversation 11 ---
Man: Excuse me, I'm looking for the history section. I need a book on ancient Rome.
Woman: The history section is on the second floor, aisle 4. Ancient Rome would be around the middle of the aisle, under the 937 call numbers.
Man: Thank you. Also, do you have a study room available? I need a quiet place to work for a couple of hours.
Woman: Let me check. We have Study Room C available from now until 4 PM. You'll need your library card to sign in.
Man: I have my card right here. Is there a time limit?
Woman: The maximum is two hours, but if no one is waiting, you can renew for an additional hour. Wi-Fi is free throughout the building.
Man: Great. And is there a place to get coffee nearby?
Woman: There's a cafe on the ground floor, right next to the main entrance.

--- Conversation 12 ---
Woman: David, I received the inspection report for the warehouse on Fifth Street. There are several issues we need to address.
Man: How serious are they?
Woman: The fire suppression system needs to be updated, and two emergency exits are blocked by storage containers. Those are the critical ones.
Man: The blocked exits need to be fixed immediately. I'll have the maintenance team clear them today. How long will the fire system update take?
Woman: The contractor said about three days. They can start next Monday. The total cost is around $4,500.
Man: That's within the maintenance budget. Go ahead and schedule them. What about the other issues?
Woman: There are some minor electrical repairs and a cracked window, but those can wait until next month.
Man: Okay, let's prioritize the fire system and the exits. I'll need a full report for the safety committee meeting on Friday.

--- Conversation 13 ---
Man: Hi, I'm interested in opening a business account. I just started a small consulting firm.
Woman: Congratulations! We have several business account options. Do you have your business registration documents and tax ID?
Man: Yes, I have them right here. What are the different account types?
Woman: We have a basic business checking with no minimum balance and a $15 monthly fee, or a premium account with a $5,000 minimum that waives the fee and includes free wire transfers.
Man: I think the basic account is fine for now. I can always upgrade later, right?
Woman: Absolutely. You can upgrade at any time. I'll also need two forms of personal ID. The process takes about 30 minutes.
Man: I have my driver's license and passport. Will I get a debit card today?
Woman: Yes, you'll receive a temporary card today, and the permanent one will be mailed within 7 to 10 business days.

sections.title: Part 4: Talks
sections.instructions: You will hear 10 short talks. Each talk will be spoken only one time and will not be printed in your test book. You will be asked to answer three questions about what is said. Select the best response to each question.
sections.transcript:
Narrator: Directions: You will hear some short talks given by a single speaker. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speaker says in each talk. Select the best response to each question.

--- Talk 1 ---
Announcer: Attention passengers, this is the final boarding call for Flight 847 to Boston departing from Gate 12. All passengers should proceed to the gate immediately as the doors will close in five minutes. Please have your boarding pass and identification ready. This is the final call for Flight 847 to Boston.

--- Talk 2 ---
Woman: Good morning, everyone. Before we begin today's training session, I'd like to go over a few housekeeping items. The restrooms are located down the hall to your left. In case of an emergency, exits are at the front and back of the room. Coffee and refreshments are available in the lobby during the break at 10:30. Please turn off or silence your mobile phones. We'll be covering three modules today: workplace safety, data security, and customer relations. Each module will take approximately 45 minutes.

--- Talk 3 ---
Man: Thank you for calling Westside Dental. Our office is open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 5 PM, and Saturdays from 9 AM to 1 PM. We are currently accepting new patients. To schedule an appointment, press 1. For billing questions, press 2. To speak with a dental hygienist, press 3. For all other inquiries, please stay on the line and a representative will be with you shortly. Thank you.

--- Talk 4 ---
Woman: This is a reminder that the annual company picnic will be held next Saturday at Riverside Park from 11 AM to 4 PM. Employees are encouraged to bring their families. There will be food, games, and a raffle with great prizes. Please RSVP by Wednesday so we can finalize the catering order. If you'd like to volunteer to help set up, please contact Sarah in Human Resources. In the event of rain, the picnic will be moved to the following Saturday.

--- Talk 5 ---
Man: Welcome to the City Art Museum. Our current exhibition features works from the Impressionist period, including pieces by Monet, Renoir, and Degas. The exhibition runs through the end of the month. Guided tours are available daily at 11 AM and 2 PM at no additional cost. Audio guides can be rented at the front desk for $5. Photography is not permitted in the special exhibition area. The museum cafe is open from 10 AM to 5 PM, and the gift shop closes at 6 PM.

--- Talk 6 ---
Woman: Attention shoppers, we have a lost child in the store. A boy named Timmy, approximately five years old, wearing a red shirt and blue jeans, is waiting at the customer service desk on the first floor. Would his parent or guardian please come to the customer service desk to pick him up? Thank you.

--- Talk 7 ---
Man: Good evening, this is your weather forecast for the week. Tomorrow will be partly cloudy with a high of 72 degrees and a low of 58. There's a 30% chance of scattered showers in the afternoon. Wednesday will be sunny and warm, reaching 78 degrees. Thursday and Friday will see temperatures in the mid-80s with increasing humidity. A cold front is expected to arrive on Saturday, bringing thunderstorms and cooler temperatures in the upper 60s. Sunday should clear up with sunny skies and a high of 70.

--- Talk 8 ---
Woman: Thank you for attending today's webinar on time management in the workplace. In this session, we covered three key strategies: prioritizing tasks using the Eisenhower Matrix, setting time blocks for focused work, and minimizing distractions. The slides and a recording of this webinar will be emailed to all registered participants within 24 hours. For those who would like a certificate of completion, please complete the short survey at the end of the session. If you have any questions, feel free to email us at the address shown on your screen.

--- Talk 9 ---
Man: This is an important announcement for all residents of the Oakwood Apartments. Starting next Monday, the water supply will be temporarily shut off from 9 AM to 3 PM for scheduled maintenance of the building's plumbing system. Please store enough water for your needs during this period. The management apologizes for any inconvenience. sections.title: Part 3: Conversations
sections.instructions: You will hear 13 conversations between two or three people. Each conversation will be spoken only one time and will not be printed in your test book. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say. Select the best response to each question.
sections.transcript:
Narrator: Directions: You will hear some conversations between two or three people. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say in each conversation. Select the best response to each question.

--- Conversation 1 ---
Man: Hi, I'd like to rent a car for the weekend. What do you have available?
Woman: We have a compact for $35 a day, a midsize for $45, and a full-size SUV for $65. All come with unlimited mileage.
Man: I'll take the midsize. Do I need to return it with a full tank?
Woman: Yes, we provide the car with a full tank and you need to return it the same way. Otherwise, there's a refueling charge of $8 per gallon.
Man: Got it. I also need a child safety seat. Is that available?
Woman: Yes, child seats are $10 per day. I'll add one to your reservation. Can I see your driver's license and a credit card?
Man: Sure, here you go. What time do I need to return the car on Sunday?
Woman: Return is by 5 PM on Sunday. There's a one-hour grace period, but after that, you'll be charged for an extra day.

--- Conversation 2 ---
Woman: Paul, I noticed the monthly sales figures dropped in the southern region. What's going on?
Man: I've been looking into it. The main issue is that our main competitor opened two new stores in the area last month, and they're offering aggressive discounts.
Woman: That's concerning. How much are they discounting?
Man: About 20% below our prices on key items. We can't match that without hurting our margins.
Woman: What do you suggest we do?
Man: I think we should focus on customer loyalty rather than competing on price. We could launch a rewards program and emphasize our superior customer service.
Woman: That's a good strategy. Can you put together a proposal by next Wednesday? I'll present it to the board on Friday.
Man: Absolutely. I'll have a detailed plan with cost estimates ready for you by Wednesday morning.

--- Conversation 3 ---
Man: Excuse me, I'm looking for a birthday gift for my wife. She mentioned she wanted a new watch.
Woman: We have a great selection. Are you looking for a specific style — casual, dress, or sport?
Man: Something elegant, maybe for the office. She wears a lot of silver jewelry.
Woman: In that case, this silver watch with a mother-of-pearl face might be perfect. It's $240, and it comes with a two-year warranty.
Man: That's beautiful. Does it have a date display?
Woman: Yes, it does. It's also water-resistant up to 30 meters. Would you like me to engrave a message on the back? We offer free engraving.
Man: That would be wonderful. Can you engrave 'Happy Birthday, Love John'?
Woman: Of course. It'll take about 15 minutes. You can browse the store while you wait.

--- Conversation 4 ---
Woman: I'm calling about the job posting for the marketing coordinator position. Is it still open?
Man: Yes, we're still accepting applications. The deadline is this Friday. Are you interested in applying?
Woman: I am. What are the main qualifications you're looking for?
Man: We need someone with at least three years of marketing experience, proficiency in social media management, and strong writing skills. A degree in marketing or communications is preferred.
Woman: I have four years of experience and a degree in communications. Where should I send my resume?
Man: You can email it to careers@company.com or apply through our website. We'll start scheduling interviews next Monday.
Woman: Great. I'll submit my application today. What's the salary range, if you don't mind me asking?
Man: The range is $50,000 to $60,000, depending on experience. We also offer health insurance and a retirement plan.

--- Conversation 5 ---
Man: Good afternoon, I'm here for my 2 o'clock appointment with Mr. Thompson.
Woman: Welcome. You must be Mr. Lee. Please have a seat. Mr. Thompson is running about ten minutes behind schedule.
Man: No problem. While I wait, could I get a glass of water?
Woman: Of course. There's also coffee and tea in the corner. Help yourself.
Man: Thank you. By the way, I need to leave by 3:30 for another meeting. Will that be an issue?
Woman: I don't think so. Mr. Thompson's meetings usually last about 30 minutes. I'll let him know you have a time constraint.
Man: I appreciate that. Also, I brought the documents he requested. Should I leave them with you?
Woman: Yes, I'll make sure they're on his desk before he calls you in.

--- Conversation 6 ---
Woman: Hey Steve, did you see the email about the office relocation? We're moving to the new building in December.
Man: Yes, I saw it. I'm a bit concerned about the commute. The new office is farther from my house.
Woman: Really? How much longer will it take you?
Man: About 20 minutes more each way. I'm thinking about switching to public transit.
Woman: That might be a good idea. The new building is right next to the metro station. Plus, the company is offering a transit subsidy of $100 a month.
Man: I didn't know about the subsidy. That helps. What about parking?
Woman: There's an underground garage, but it's $120 a month. Only managers get free parking.
Man: I'll definitely take the metro then. When exactly do we move in?
Woman: December 15th. The IT team will set up our equipment over the weekend before.

--- Conversation 7 ---
Man: I'd like to book a table for four at 7 PM this Saturday.
Woman: Let me check. We do have availability. Would you prefer indoor or outdoor seating?
Man: Indoor, please. It might be chilly in the evening.
Woman: No problem. Can I get a name for the reservation?
Man: It's under Martinez. Could we also get a table near the window if possible?
Woman: I'll note that as a preference, but I can't guarantee it. We get very busy on Saturday nights. Is this for a special occasion?
Man: Yes, it's my parents' anniversary. Could you have a small dessert brought to the table with a candle?
Woman: Absolutely, we'd be happy to do that. I'll add a note for the kitchen. There's no charge for the dessert — it's on the house for special occasions.
Man: That's very kind. Thank you so much.

--- Conversation 8 ---
Woman: Professor Davis, I wanted to talk to you about my research paper. I'm having trouble finding enough sources.
Man: Which topic did you choose, again?
Woman: I'm writing about the impact of social media on small businesses. The library database doesn't have much on that specific angle.
Man: I see. Have you tried the business research database? It has journals that the main library doesn't carry. You can access it through the university portal.
Woman: I didn't know about that. I'll check it out. Also, is it okay if I extend my paper to 12 pages? I feel like I need more space.
Man: The requirement is 8 to 10 pages, but I'll allow up to 12 if it's well-structured. Don't add filler, though. Quality over quantity.
Woman: Understood. When is the final deadline for submission?
Man: The paper is due on the 20th. I can give you a two-day extension if you need it, but no more than that.

--- Conversation 9 ---
Man: Hi, I need to get my car inspected. The registration expires at the end of the month.
Woman: Sure, we can do that. Is this for the annual safety inspection?
Man: Yes, and I also need an emissions test. I have the renewal notice from the DMV.
Woman: Perfect. The safety inspection is $35 and the emissions test is $25. The whole process takes about 45 minutes. Do you want to wait or drop it off?
Man: I'll wait. Is there a place nearby to grab a coffee?
Woman: There's a cafe two doors down. We'll call you when it's ready. Can I get your phone number?
Man: It's 555-0182. By the way, if something fails, how long do I have to fix it?
Woman: You have 30 days to repair any issues and get a re-inspection at no additional cost. But if it's past 30 days, you'll need to pay for a full inspection again.

--- Conversation 10 ---
Woman: Michael, I need your input on the new product packaging design. We have two options.
Man: Sure, let me take a look. I like the blue one — it's more modern and eye-catching.
Woman: I agree it looks better, but it costs 15% more to produce. The budget is already tight.
Man: How much more per unit?
Woman: About 30 cents more per package. Over 50,000 units, that adds up to $15,000.
Man: That is significant. But if the better design increases sales by even 5%, it would more than offset the cost. Do we have any market research on this?
Woman: Actually, the marketing team did a focus group last month. 70% of participants preferred the blue design.
Man: Then I think we should go with it. Can you adjust the budget and present the numbers to the director?
Woman: I'll have the revised budget ready by Thursday and schedule a meeting with the director for Friday.

--- Conversation 11 ---
Man: I'm thinking about enrolling in the evening MBA program. What do you think?
Woman: That's a big commitment. Classes are two nights a week for two years. Are you sure you can balance that with work?
Man: I've been thinking about it for a while. My manager is supportive and said I can adjust my hours on class days.
Woman: That's good. Have you looked at the tuition? It's about $45,000 for the full program.
Man: I know. But the company has a tuition reimbursement program that covers up to $10,000 per year.
Woman: That helps a lot. You should also check if any of your previous coursework transfers. That could save you time and money.
Man: Good idea. I'll contact the admissions office about transfer credits. When does the next cohort start?
Woman: The fall semester begins in September. The application deadline is June 1st, so you have about two months to apply.

--- Conversation 12 ---
Woman: We need to talk about the upcoming trade show in Las Vegas. Have you finalized the booth design?
Man: Almost. The design team sent over three concepts. I like the second one — it has an interactive display and a demo station.
Woman: I agree. What about the promotional materials? Do we have enough brochures and giveaways?
Man: I ordered 2,000 brochures and 500 branded tote bags. They should arrive by next Tuesday.
Woman: Great. How many staff members are going?
Man: Five of us — you, me, and three from the sales team. I've booked flights and the hotel. The total travel budget is $8,500.
Woman: That's within our allocation. Don't forget to register for the networking dinner on the first night. It's a great opportunity to make contacts.
Man: Already done. I've also scheduled a team briefing for the day before we leave to go over our pitch and objectives.

--- Conversation 13 ---
Man: Hi, I'm here to pick up my prescription. The name is Robert Chen.
Woman: Let me look that up. Yes, I have it right here. That'll be $25. Your insurance covered most of it.
Man: That's less than I expected. When should I take the medication?
Woman: Take one tablet twice a day, with meals. Morning and evening. Don't take it on an empty stomach.
Man: Got it. Are there any side effects I should know about?
Woman: The most common ones are drowsiness and dry mouth. Avoid driving if you feel drowsy. Also, don't drink alcohol while taking this medication.
Man: Understood. How many days is the prescription for?
Woman: It's a 14-day supply. You should start feeling better within 3 to 5 days, but finish the entire prescription even if you feel fine. Do you have any other questions?
Man: No, that's everything. Thank you.

--- Talk 1 ---
Man: Attention all staff, this is a reminder that the annual fire drill will take place tomorrow at 10 AM. When the alarm sounds, please leave your workstations immediately and exit through the nearest emergency exit. Do not use the elevators. Assembly points are in the parking lot behind the building. Department heads should take attendance and report to the safety officer. The drill should take no more than 20 minutes, after which you may return to your workstations.

--- Talk 2 ---
Woman: Welcome to the Grandview Hotel. Check-in is at 3 PM and check-out is by 11 AM. Complimentary breakfast is served in the dining room from 6:30 to 9:30 AM. The fitness center is open 24 hours, and the pool is open from 6 AM to 10 PM. Wi-Fi is free throughout the hotel, and the password is printed on your room key card. If you need extra towels or toiletries, please call the front desk. Valet parking is available for $25 per day.

--- Talk 3 ---
Man: This is the 6 o'clock news. In business today, the stock market closed higher, with the Dow Jones up 150 points. Tech stocks led the gains, with several companies reporting better-than-expected earnings. In international news, a trade agreement was signed between two major economies, which is expected to reduce tariffs on electronics and agricultural products. Locally, a new community center will open in the downtown area next month, offering free classes for residents. The weather tomorrow will be sunny with a high of 75 degrees.

--- Talk 4 ---
Woman: Thank you for calling Greenfield Medical Center. Our office hours are Monday through Friday, 7 AM to 7 PM, and Saturday from 8 AM to 2 PM. We are closed on Sundays. For appointments, press 1. For prescription refills, press 2. For the billing department, press 3. If this is a medical emergency, please hang up and dial 911. For all other questions, stay on the line and a representative will assist you. Thank you.

--- Talk 5 ---
Man: Good afternoon, passengers. This is your captain speaking. We've reached our cruising altitude of 36,000 feet. We expect some light turbulence as we pass over the mountains, so I've turned on the fasten seatbelt sign. Please return to your seats and fasten your seatbelts. We should be through the rough air in about 20 minutes. Our estimated arrival time in Denver is 4:15 PM, which is about 10 minutes ahead of schedule. The current temperature in Denver is 68 degrees.

--- Talk 6 ---
Woman: Attention shoppers, today's special in the deli department features a buy-one-get-one-free offer on all fresh sandwiches. In the produce section, organic apples are on sale for $1.99 per pound. Don't forget to pick up today's bakery special: fresh croissants at 3 for $5. The sale ends at closing time, which is 9 PM. Our loyalty card members receive an additional 5% off all purchases today. Sign up at the customer service desk — it's free.

--- Talk 7 ---
Man: Welcome to the National History Museum. Our dinosaur exhibit has been extended through the end of next month due to popular demand. The planetarium show runs every hour on the hour from 10 AM to 4 PM. Tickets are $8 for adults and $4 for children under 12. Members get free admission to all exhibits and shows. The museum cafe is located on the second floor and is open from 9 AM to 5 PM. Please note that large bags and backpacks must be stored in the lockers near the entrance. Lockers require a 25-cent deposit.

--- Talk 8 ---
Woman: This is a message for all employees from the Human Resources department. Open enrollment for benefits begins on Monday and runs for two weeks. During this period, you can make changes to your health insurance, dental plan, and retirement contributions. Information packets have been sent to your company email. Please review the materials carefully, as this is the only time you can make changes unless you experience a qualifying life event. A representative from the benefits provider will be on-site on Wednesday and Thursday to answer questions.

--- Talk 9 ---
Man: Good evening, and welcome to tonight's performance of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream.' The show will begin in approximately ten minutes. Please take your seats and silence all electronic devices. Photography and recording are strictly prohibited during the performance. The running time is two hours and thirty minutes, including a 15-minute intermission. Refreshments are available in the lobby. If you have an aisle seat, please keep the aisle clear for safety. Thank you, and enjoy the show.

--- Talk 10 ---
Woman: Welcome to the 2024 Small Business Expo. Today's event features over 50 local businesses showcasing their products and services. The expo hall is open from 10 AM to 6 PM. At 1 PM, there will be a keynote address by entrepreneur Sarah Chen in the main auditorium. Free workshops on marketing, finance, and technology will be held in Rooms A, B, and C throughout the day. Food trucks are located outside the east entrance. Don't forget to pick up your raffle ticket at the entrance for a chance to win a $500 gift card. The raffle drawing will be held at 5:30 PM.

Narrator: Directions: You will hear some conversations between two or three people. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speakers say in each conversation. Select the best response to each question.

--- Conversation 1 ---
Man: Hi, I'm calling about the job I applied for — the software developer position. I had an interview two weeks ago.
Woman: Let me check. Yes, I see your application, Mr. Park. The interview panel has completed their evaluation. We'd like to offer you the position.
Man: That's wonderful news! When would I start?
Woman: We'd like you to start on the 15th of next month. The starting salary is $75,000 per year, with a review after six months. You'll also receive full health benefits and 15 days of paid vacation.
Man: That sounds great. Is there a signing bonus?
Woman: Yes, there's a $3,000 signing bonus, payable after your first 90 days. I'll send the official offer letter by email today. You'll need to sign and return it within five business days.
Man: I'll look out for it. Thank you so much!

--- Conversation 2 ---
Woman: David, I need to discuss the inventory shortage we discovered during the audit. We're missing about 200 units of product A.
Man: That's significant. When was the last time the inventory was checked?
Woman: The last full count was three months ago. The shortage could be due to a logging error or, worse, theft.
Man: Let's not jump to conclusions. Have you checked the shipping records? Sometimes items are in transit but not properly logged.
Woman: I'm looking at them now. It looks like a shipment of 150 units was sent to the west coast warehouse but wasn't recorded in our system.
Man: That accounts for most of it. What about the remaining 50 units?
Woman: I think those might be in the returns area — items that came back from customers but haven't been restocked yet. I'll go check after this meeting.
Man: Good. Let's also implement weekly spot checks going forward to prevent this from happening again.

--- Conversation 3 ---
Man: Excuse me, I'm looking for a suit for a job interview. I need something professional but not too expensive.
Woman: We have a great selection in the $300 to $500 range. What size are you?
Man: I'm a 40 regular. I'd prefer something in navy or dark gray.
Woman: Let me show you this navy pinstripe. It's $350 and includes a jacket and trousers. It's one of our best sellers.
Man: I like it. Can I try it on? Also, do you do alterations?
Woman: Absolutely. The fitting room is right over there. We offer free alterations on suits, including hemming and waist adjustments. It usually takes 2 to 3 days.
Man: Perfect. If I buy it today, could I pick it up by Thursday? My interview is on Friday morning.
Woman: Thursday should be no problem. Let me note the rush on your order.

--- Conversation 4 ---
Woman: I'm thinking about switching to the new phone plan. The one with unlimited data. Can you tell me about it?
Man: Sure. The unlimited plan is $65 per month. It includes unlimited talk, text, and 5G data. You also get a free subscription to our streaming service.
Woman: That sounds good. I'm currently paying $50 for 10 gigabytes. What happens if I go over?
Man: With your current plan, you're charged $10 per extra gigabyte. With the unlimited plan, there are no overage charges. However, after 50 gigabytes, data speeds may be reduced during peak hours.
Woman: I see. Is there a contract?
Man: No, it's month-to-month. You can cancel anytime without a penalty. If you switch today, we'll also waive the $25 activation fee.
Woman: That's a good deal. Let me think about it and come back tomorrow.

--- Conversation 5 ---
Man: Good morning, I'd like to open a savings account. What are the current interest rates?
Woman: We have two options. The standard savings account offers 0.5% APY with no minimum balance. The high-yield account offers 2.5% APY but requires a minimum balance of $10,000.
Man: The high-yield sounds better. Is there a monthly fee?
Woman: There's no monthly fee as long as you maintain the $10,000 minimum. If the balance falls below that, there's a $15 monthly fee. You also get six free withdrawals per month.
Man: I can maintain the minimum. What do I need to open the account?
Woman: I'll need two forms of ID, like a driver's license and a passport, and your initial deposit. The process takes about 20 minutes. You'll also get a debit card linked to the account.
Man: I have my license and passport. The initial deposit will be $15,000. Can I transfer it from my checking account?
Woman: Yes, we can do an electronic transfer. Let me get the paperwork started.

--- Conversation 6 ---
Woman: Hey Tom, did you see the memo about the new remote work policy? Starting next month, we can work from home two days a week.
Man: I saw that. It's a nice change. Do we need to specify which days in advance?
Woman: Yes, we need to submit our preferred days to our manager by Friday each week for the following week. The days should be consistent.
Man: I was thinking Tuesdays and Thursdays. What about you?
Woman: I'm planning on Mondays and Wednesdays. That way, we're in the office on the same days for meetings.
Man: Good idea. Do we need any special equipment at home? I don't have a company laptop.
Woman: IT is providing laptops to everyone who needs one. You just need to submit a request through the portal. They'll also set up a VPN so you can access the network securely.
Man: Great. I'll submit the request today. Are there any restrictions on where we can work from?
Woman: You need to be within a 50-mile radius of the office, and you need a reliable internet connection.

--- Conversation 7 ---
Man: I'd like to send this package to Singapore. What are the shipping options?
Woman: We have express shipping, which takes 2 to 3 business days and costs $85. Standard shipping takes 7 to 10 business days and costs $35.
Man: I need it there by Friday. Today is Tuesday, so express would work. Does that include tracking?
Woman: Yes, both options include tracking and insurance up to $100. If the package value is higher, you can purchase additional insurance for $5 per $100 of value.
Man: The contents are worth about $300, so I'll add $10 in insurance. Do I need to fill out a customs form?
Woman: Yes, since it's an international shipment, you'll need to complete a customs declaration form. I have one right here. It asks for the contents, value, and purpose of the shipment.
Man: It's a gift — some books and clothing. Let me fill that out. Can I pay with a credit card?
Woman: Of course. The total comes to $95 — $85 for shipping plus $10 for insurance.

--- Conversation 8 ---
Woman: Professor, I'm having trouble with the calculus assignment. I don't understand how to solve the optimization problems.
Man: Which section are you working on?
Woman: Section 4.3, the ones about maximizing area and minimizing cost. I get the derivatives, but I'm not sure how to set up the initial equations.
Man: The key is to identify what you're optimizing and what your constraint is. Let me show you an example. If you're maximizing the area of a rectangle with a fixed perimeter, you first express the area in terms of one variable.
Woman: Oh, I see. So I use the constraint to eliminate one variable, then take the derivative and set it to zero?
Man: Exactly. Then you solve for the critical point and verify it's a maximum or minimum using the second derivative test. I have office hours on Thursday from 2 to 4 PM if you'd like more help.
Woman: I'll come by on Thursday. Are there any additional practice problems I can work on before then?
Man: Check the textbook — problems 15 through 20 in section 4.3 are good practice. Also, the math tutoring center on the third floor is open Monday through Friday from 10 AM to 6 PM.

--- Conversation 9 ---
Man: Hi, I'm here for the 3 PM tour of the facility. My name is Brian Foster.
Woman: Welcome, Mr. Foster. I'm Rachel, and I'll be your guide today. The tour takes about 45 minutes and covers the main production floor, the quality control lab, and the warehouse.
Man: Sounds great. I'm particularly interested in your quality control processes. How do you ensure product consistency?
Woman: We have a three-stage inspection process. Raw materials are tested on arrival, products are checked during manufacturing, and a final inspection is done before packaging. We also do random batch testing.
Man: That's impressive. What's your defect rate?
Woman: Currently, it's under 0.5%, which is well below the industry average. We also have a continuous improvement program where we analyze any defects and adjust our processes.
Man: Do you offer tours to potential clients regularly?
Woman: Yes, we schedule tours twice a week — Tuesdays and Thursdays at 3 PM. For existing clients, we can arrange custom tours. Would you like to see the production floor first?
Man: Yes, let's start there.

--- Conversation 10 ---
Woman: I received the contract from the vendor, but I have some concerns about the payment terms.
Man: What specifically are you concerned about?
Woman: They want 50% upfront before any work begins, and the remaining 50% within 30 days of delivery. That's a lot of money to commit before seeing any results.
Man: I agree. Let's negotiate. We could propose 30% upfront, 40% upon delivery, and 30% after 30 days of testing. That gives us some leverage.
Woman: That's a good counteroffer. What about the delivery timeline? They said 12 weeks, but our project deadline is in 10 weeks.
Man: We need to push for a 9-week delivery to give us a week for integration. If they can't meet that, we should look at other vendors.
Woman: I'll draft a counter-proposal and send it to them today. Should I cc you on the email?
Man: Yes, please. Also, let's set a deadline for their response — 48 hours. If they don't agree by Thursday, we move on.

--- Conversation 11 ---
Man: I'm looking to book a flight to Paris for next month. What's available?
Woman: I can help with that. What dates are you looking at, and is this a round trip?
Man: Round trip, departing March 10th and returning March 17th. I'd prefer a morning departure.
Woman: We have a flight departing at 8:30 AM on the 10th, with a layover in London. The return flight on the 17th departs Paris at 2 PM. The total fare is $780.
Man: Is there a direct flight available?
Woman: There is a direct flight at 10 AM, but it's $1,150. The layover in London is only 90 minutes, so the total travel time is about 2 hours longer.
Man: I'll take the one with the layover. Can I choose my seats?
Woman: Yes, seat selection is free for this fare. Would you like a window or aisle seat?
Man: Aisle seat, please. Also, how many bags can I check?
Woman: The fare includes one free checked bag up to 50 pounds. A second bag is $60. Carry-on is included at no charge.

--- Conversation 12 ---
Woman: The marketing team has finalized the campaign for the new product launch. Can we go over the timeline?
Man: Sure. The campaign starts with a teaser on social media on the 1st, followed by the official launch event on the 5th. Print and digital ads begin on the 6th and run for four weeks.
Woman: What about the influencer partnerships?
Man: We've secured five influencers who will post on the 5th and 6th, coinciding with the launch event. Their combined reach is about 2 million followers.
Woman: That's great exposure. What's the total budget?
Man: The total campaign budget is $150,000. That includes $40,000 for the launch event, $60,000 for digital and print ads, $30,000 for influencer partnerships, and $20,000 for creative production.
Woman: The board approved $140,000. We're $10,000 over. Can we trim anything?
Man: I can reduce the print ad spend by $10,000 and shift more to digital, which is more cost-effective. I'll revise the budget and send it to you by end of day.

--- Conversation 13 ---
Man: Hi, I need to get a new pair of eyeglasses. My prescription has changed.
Woman: Have you had an eye exam recently, or do you have a current prescription?
Man: I had an exam last month. Here's the prescription from my optometrist.
Woman: Thank you. Let me help you pick out frames. We have designer frames starting at $150 and budget options from $60. Your insurance covers up to $200 for frames and $80 for lenses.
Man: I'd like something durable. What about these titanium frames?
Woman: Those are $220. With your $200 allowance, you'd pay $20 out of pocket for the frames. For the lenses, would you like standard, anti-glare, or progressive?
Man: I need progressive lenses. How much are those?
Woman: Progressive lenses are $280. With your $80 lens allowance, that's $200 out of pocket. So your total would be $220 — $20 for frames and $200 for lenses. The eye exam is fully covered.
Man: That works. How long will it take to get them?
Woman: About 7 to 10 business days. We'll call you when they're ready for pickup.

sections.title: Part 4: Talks
sections.instructions: You will hear 10 short talks. Each talk will be spoken only one time and will not be printed in your test book. You will be asked to answer three questions about what is said. Select the best response to each question.
sections.transcript:
Narrator: Directions: You will hear some short talks given by a single speaker. You will be asked to answer three questions about what the speaker says in each talk. Select the best response to each question.

--- Talk 1 ---
Man: Attention, everyone. Due to severe weather conditions, the company has decided to close the office at 1 PM today. All non-essential employees should head home. Essential staff should check with their supervisors for further instructions. The office will reopen tomorrow at the regular time, weather permitting. Please check your email or the company website for updates. Stay safe, and thank you for your cooperation.

--- Talk 2 ---
Woman: Welcome to the orientation session for new employees. My name is Karen, and I'm from Human Resources. Today, we'll cover several important topics. First, I'll explain the company's code of conduct and ethics policy. Then, we'll review the benefits package, including health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off. After a short break, IT will walk you through setting up your email and accessing the company network. Finally, you'll meet with your department heads for a brief introduction. The session should conclude by 4 PM, and lunch will be provided in the cafeteria.

--- Talk 3 ---
Man: This is a public service announcement. The city's water department will be conducting routine maintenance on the main water line this Saturday from 6 AM to 2 PM. Residents in the downtown area may experience low water pressure or temporary shutoffs during this time. It's recommended to store water for drinking and cooking beforehand. If you experience any issues after 2 PM, please call the water department's 24-hour hotline at 555-0100. We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate your patience.

--- Talk 4 ---
Woman: Thank you for calling the City Library. Our hours are Monday through Thursday, 9 AM to 9 PM; Friday and Saturday, 9 AM to 5 PM; and Sunday, 1 PM to 5 PM. To renew books, press 1. To check on hold requests, press 2. For information about upcoming events, press 3. To speak with a librarian, press 0. You can also access our catalog and manage your account online at www.citylibrary.org. Thank you, and have a great day.

--- Talk 5 ---
Man: Good morning, this is your bus driver speaking. We'll be arriving at the central station in approximately 15 minutes. Please gather your belongings and prepare to exit. The front and rear doors will both be available for exiting. If you need to transfer to another bus, transfer tickets are available at no charge — just ask me as you exit. Please remember to take all personal items with you. The next bus to the airport departs from Platform 3 every 20 minutes. Thank you for riding with us today.

--- Talk 6 ---
Woman: Welcome to today's seminar on workplace communication. I'm Dr. Emily Roberts, and I'll be your facilitator. Effective communication is the foundation of any successful organization. Today, we'll explore three key areas: active listening, giving and receiving feedback, and cross-cultural communication in diverse workplaces. The seminar is interactive, so please participate freely. Handouts are in the folder in front of you. We'll take a 15-minute break at 10:30, and lunch will be served at 12:30 in the adjacent room. The seminar concludes at 3 PM, and certificates will be distributed at that time.

--- Talk 7 ---
Man: Attention, passengers on Track 4. The 5:15 PM express train to Chicago has been delayed by approximately 30 minutes due to a signal issue. The train is now expected to depart at 5:45 PM. We apologize for the inconvenience. Passengers with connecting trains should speak with a customer service representative at the ticket counter. The next train to Chicago, the 6:00 PM local, is running on time if you'd prefer to take that instead. Refreshments are available at the concession stand in the main waiting area. Thank you for your patience.

--- Talk 8 ---
Woman: This is a reminder that the deadline for submitting your self-assessment forms is this Friday at 5 PM. All employees must complete the self-assessment as part of the annual performance review process. Please be thorough and honest in your responses. Your manager will review your self-assessment before your scheduled review meeting. If you have not yet scheduled your review meeting, please do so with your manager by Wednesday. Late submissions will not be accepted without prior approval from your department head. If you have questions, please contact HR.

--- Talk 9 ---
Man: Welcome to the Riverside Fitness Center. Our facility features a fully equipped gym, an Olympic-size swimming pool, three tennis courts, and a group exercise studio. Membership options include a monthly plan at $60 per month with no commitment, or an annual plan at $600, which saves you $120. We also offer a couples' plan at $90 per month. Your first personal training session is complimentary. Group classes like yoga, spin, and Pilates are included with all memberships. The pool is open from 5 AM to 9 PM, and the gym is open 24 hours for members. Lockers and towels are provided at no extra cost.

--- Talk 10 ---
Woman: Good evening, and thank you for coming to tonight's charity auction. All proceeds from tonight's event will go to the Children's Education Fund, which provides scholarships and school supplies to underprivileged children. We have over 100 items up for auction, including vacation packages, artwork, and sports memorabilia. Bidding starts at 7 PM, and the auction closes at 10 PM. Payment can be made by cash, check, or credit card. If you win an item, please pick it up at the collection desk before leaving. Light refreshments are served in the back. Thank you for your generosity and support.
